name: Filter press; wastewater treatment unit; flat glass industry; at plant
description: This unit process reflects  for U.S. flat glass production facilities. The functional unit reflects treatment of 1 cubic meter of wastewater from a relevant facility. The scope of this process is limited to . Use the corresponding wastewater treatment process to reflect the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Inventory data based on technical specifications for filter press equipment available in 2025.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: A dewatering device that uses a hydraulic power unit to expel water from wastewater sludge. Slurry is pumped into the press, where solids are captured on the cloths, forming a filter cake, while clarified liquid passes through the cloth and exits as filtrate.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Assume a facility size of 1 MGD. The quantity of sludge generated was estimated assuming influent and final TSS values of 15 and 5, respectively. The solids content of clarifier underflow is 4% (2-6% range). The filter press operates 6 cycles per day (6-8 hours) and produces a final cake with a 30% solids content (25-35% range). Estimated power consumption assumes a 50 minute cycle time. The hydraulic power unit (1.1 kW) operates for the duration of the cycle. The feed pump (3 kW) operates for 30 minutes per cycle. The air compressor operates for four minutes per cycle. 0.92 m3 of sludge is produced per day which results in 103 liters of sludge cake, following dewatering.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Exclusion of mechanical and electrical equipment from the system boundary is the only known missing, non-trivial inventory item. Sludge generation was estimated based on a TSS mass balance. No other mass balance was performed.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Inventory data was developed using recent (2025) technical specifications, per the assumptions described in the modeling constants field. The electricity estimate (0.422 kWh/kg solids) was developed using bottom-up calculations, for a more granular understanding of power consumption, and compared to literature estimates (range = 0.03-0.61 kWh/kg solids). Polymer dose was set equal to the median (7.5 g/kg solids) of the identified range (range = 3.7-10 g/kg solids).
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: LCI data is reported on an annual (energy, chemicals) or lifetime (infrastructure) basis. Annual quantities are standardized to the functional unit by dividing by the average quantity of wastewater treated per year. For inventory data reported on a lifetime basis, quantities are standardized to the functional unit by amortizing the inventory item over the expected lifespan of the infrastructure component. Filter press lifespans was assumed to be 15 years. Filter plate lifespan was assumed to be 5 years.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The scope of this treatment process includes basic infrastructure, electricity and chemical requirements.  Infrastructure disposal and electrical and mechanical equipment are outside of the system boundaries.  Uncertainty ranges are provided for the electricity and polymer flows based on min/max values identified in a limited literature review.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process reflects only the impact of a single wastewater treatment process.  Use one of the corresponding wastewater treatment systems to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication: This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public to model wastewater treatment plant construction and operation. This process needs to be used in combination with other wastewater treatment processes, sludge management processes and an effluent release process to model the full scope of wastewater impacts. The inventory should be sufficient to model TRACI 2.1 impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: This unit process was prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) on behalf of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory as part of their Federal LCA Commons curation activities.
